title: Parsing Multiple Numbers
story: A form on your website has three fields: age, score, and quantity. Users might leave some blank or type junk. You need to parse all three and report how many were valid — without crashing on the bad ones.
why: Real applications process multiple inputs at once — parsing each with Result and aggregating the outcomes teaches robust batch processing.
analogy: Parsing multiple numbers is like checking tickets at a concert — each person hands you a ticket; some are valid (Ok), some are fake (Err). You count how many got in.
try_it: Add a fifth input. Then change the logic so that if fewer than 2 inputs are valid, the program prints "Error: too many invalid inputs" and stops early. Test with all-valid and mostly-invalid data.
tips: `if let Ok(n) = result` lets you check success without caring about the error value
Use `Err(_)` in match to ignore the error message when you just need to know it failed
Track counts separately so you can report metrics like '3 of 5 fields were valid'
common_mistakes: Not initializing count and sum before accumulating — they must start at 0
Shadowing variables inside match — `match r1 { Ok(n) => ... }` creates a new n, it doesn't change outer variables unless you use assignment
Forgetting that each match arm is independent — variable changes in one arm don't affect the other
